title: Ethiopian Layered Pancake
community: Harar and eastern Ethiopia — the honeycomb pancake
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Mulmul — a slightly fermented wheat pancake cooked like injera (never flipped, covered to steam) producing a soft, holey, spongy bread similar to injera but made from wheat. The Harari breakfast bread — lighter than injera with a milder sourness.
longDesc: Mulmul is Harar's answer to injera — a slightly fermented wheat pancake cooked by the same covered, single-side method. It produces a softer, less sour, more tender result than teff injera, and is the traditional breakfast bread of eastern Ethiopia's Harari community.
steps: Dissolve yeast and sugar in warm water. Add flour and salt. Whisk smooth.
Cover and rest 1 hour at room temperature until slightly bubbly.
Heat pan to medium. Pour a ladleful — thin layer.
Cover immediately. Cook 2—3 minutes until surface is dry and holes have formed.
Never flip — slide off and cool.
chefTips: Thinner batter than injera — mulmul should be even more holey.
The 1-hour fermentation is a minimum — 2 hours produces more holes and flavour.
cookingScience: See ETH001 for the hole-formation science. Wheat-based mulmul forms holes more readily than teff injera because wheat gluten creates a more elastic foam structure that holds CO2 bubbles more effectively before they burst and form holes.
sustainabilityTips: Wheat-based bread accessible to those who cannot afford teff.
storage: Best eaten same day. Refrigerate 2 days.
culturalNote: Mulmul is the morning food of Harar — the ancient walled city that is one of Islam's holiest cities in Africa. The Harari breakfast tradition of mulmul with honey and spiced tea is one of Ethiopia's most refined morning rituals.
